The Chinese dynasty of the Sima family, which reunited China in 280 and ruled the south until 420. The map shows it in 300 over most of China, and in 400 in the south only.

Sima Yan took the throne from the Cao Wei in 266 and conquered the last rival state, Wu, in 280, ending the Three Kingdoms era. Unity did not last. After his death the War of the Eight Princes tore the court apart, and nomad leaders raised armies in the north. The Xiongnu state of Han Zhao sacked Luoyang in 311 and Chang'an in 316, and the north broke into the Sixteen Kingdoms.

A Jin prince refounded the dynasty at Jiankang, modern Nanjing, in 317: the Eastern Jin. Northern families joined a great flight south, and the Yangtze lands grew in wealth. The calligrapher Wang Xizhi lived under the Eastern Jin, and Buddhism spread among the elite. In 383 the Jin beat a huge northern army at the Fei River. The general Liu Yu ended the dynasty in 420.
